# Cal/OSHA Fire Safety & Emergency Evacuation Training

> 2-hour online course for California employees on fire prevention, portable fire extinguisher use (P.A.S.S. and the fight-or-flee decision), emergency action plans and evacuation procedures. Built around Title 8 CCR Section 6151 (Portable Fire Extinguishers) with Sections 3220 (Emergency Action Plan) and 3221 (Fire Prevention Plan). Offered by HAZWOPER OSHA Training (https://hazwoper-osha.com).

## Key facts
- Standards: Title 8 CCR §6151, §3220, §3221; means of egress §3215–3235; fire protection Group 27 (§6150–6184)
- Training frequency: employers providing portable extinguishers must educate employees at initial employment and at least annually; all employees briefed on the EAP and relevant FPP parts; designated firefighting staff need additional equipment training
- Fight or flee: fight only incipient-stage fires (small, confined to point of origin, controllable with a portable extinguisher or small hose); otherwise evacuate
- P.A.S.S.: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep
- Scope note: based on General Industry Safety Orders; construction sites also follow Construction Safety Orders
- Duration: 2 hours; 5 lessons plus final exam
- Credits: 0.2 CEU
- Price: $49.99 per person online; bulk pricing from 2 seats; SCORM, virtual and in-person options
- Delivery: 100% online, 24/7; English and Spanish
- Certificate: instant PDF on passing, valid 12 months
- Prerequisites: none

## Lessons
1. Fire Safety: An Overview (fire tetrahedron, heat transfer, four stages of fire, California Fire Code)
2. Fire Prevention (Fire Prevention Plan, housekeeping, flammables, ignition sources)
3. Fire Protection (extinguishers, P.A.S.S., fight-or-flee, standpipes, fixed systems, alarms)
4. Emergency Action Plans (exit routes, refuge areas, shelter-in-place, drills)
5. Emergency Evacuation Procedures (alarms, wardens, headcounts, assembly points)

## Who it is for
Office, commercial, hospitality, healthcare and lab employees; manufacturing, warehouse, construction and maintenance workers; supervisors; designated extinguisher users; evacuation wardens and response teams; hot work and flammable-materials handlers.
